sections.thesis: Treasuries sold off sharply after October consumer prices rose 0.4% against expectations of 0.3%, sparking bets the Fed will raise rates next month.

sentences.text: Treasuries sold off sharply after October consumer prices rose 0.4% against expectations of 0.3%, sparking bets the Fed will raise rates next month.
Two-year yields rose as much as 0.22 percentage points to 4.78%, and the 10-year topped 5% for the first time this month.
Fed governor Christopher Waller said if core inflation stayed at 0.3%, "hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk".
Japan's 10-year yield rose 5.9bp to 2.754% early Wednesday.

sections.thesis: New US 10-year notes sold at 5%, the most since 2006, and the yen fell to its weakest against the dollar since mid-October, just under 159.00.

sentences.text: New US 10-year notes sold at 5%, the most since 2006, and the yen fell to its weakest against the dollar since mid-October, just under 159.00.
The inflation data lifted two-year yields 19bp and revived talk of a 50bp Fed hike.
US producer prices for October are due Friday.

sections.thesis: US stocks dropped after the inflation data added to rate-rise expectations, with the S&P 500 closing 0.4% lower and the Nasdaq 100 down 0.6%.

sentences.text: US stocks dropped after the inflation data added to rate-rise expectations, with the S&P 500 closing 0.4% lower and the Nasdaq 100 down 0.6%.
Nvidia dragged on all three indexes after chief executive Jensen Huang admitted an affair with a woman accused of spying for China.
CoreWeave rose 7% after hours on results and guidance above expectations, though it guided to $1.05 billion to $1.15 billion of fourth-quarter interest.

sections.thesis: Oil fell below $90 a barrel for the first time since August after President Trump said renewed US attacks on Iran were "highly unlikely".

sentences.text: Oil fell below $90 a barrel for the first time since August after President Trump said renewed US attacks on Iran were "highly unlikely".
Brent fell as much as 3.7% to $89.16 before settling 1.2% lower at $91.49, and has fallen about 22% in November.
Prices rebounded early Wednesday, with Brent 0.75% higher at $92.19, while strikes continued around Hormuz.
